system.name: Data-flow Availability
system.one_liner: a proposed availability property and enforcement approach that propagates timing constraints consistently across the layers of autonomous cyber-physical systems

content.subject: how a Prioritize/Abort decision from one timing inconsistency is applied consistently across middleware, kernel and network schedulers

elements.name: T_k+1
elements.role: task instance A at time k+1 (pale pink Task Instance box)

elements.name: T_k (Task Instance A)
elements.role: task instance A at time k (rose Task Instance box), later prioritized

elements.name: T_k (Timing Vertex B)
elements.role: timing vertex for a task of application B (green box), the entity Tk/Tk+1 of A is compared against

elements.name: C
elements.role: comparator node that receives the task instances and timing vertex and flags a timing inconsistency

elements.name: Inconsistency
elements.role: names the condition C detects between the compared timing entities

elements.name: Prioritize
elements.role: decision outcome that boosts a schedulable entity's priority; recurs at every layer in green

elements.name: Abort
elements.role: decision outcome that cancels a schedulable entity; recurs at every layer in red

elements.name: Handler
elements.role: top-level timing-constraint-violation handler that receives the Abort/Prioritize decision

elements.name: Middleware-level Task Scheduler
elements.role: middleware layer that applies Prioritize/Abort to thread pools

elements.name: Thread Pool #1
elements.role: thread pool holding Tk (prioritized), a neutral thread, and Tk+1 (aborted)

elements.name: Thread Pool #2
elements.role: another, unaffected thread pool in the same middleware scheduler

elements.name: Kernel-level Task Scheduler
elements.role: OS layer that applies the same Prioritize/Abort decision to real-time kernel threads

elements.name: Network Packet Scheduler
elements.role: I/O layer queue that applies Prioritize to the packet belonging to the same schedulable entity

elements.name: New Packet
elements.role: incoming packet entering the network queue, prioritized ahead of others

elements.name: Decision
elements.role: a gate marking where the Prioritize/Abort instruction is applied at that layer; drawn once per layer

at each scheduling layer's Decision gate, apply Prioritize or Abort to this layer's representation of the entity (thread or packet)?

content.key_idea: A single timing-inconsistency verdict (Prioritize Tk, Abort Tk+1) is associated once and then re-applied with the same colour coding at the middleware, kernel and network layers.
content.reading_order: top: task instances and timing vertices feed the inconsistency check and Handler; then down through the Middleware, Kernel and Network scheduler boxes in turn

dusty rose fill marking Tk, the task instance that gets Prioritized, repeated in every layer
blue-gray fill of the neutral filler thread/packet blocks and the C inconsistency-check node
medium gray arrowheads and the pale Tk+1 (Abort) block outlines
dark gray body text and box borders

style.stroke: ~1.1pt strokes, a mix of solid and dashed outlines (dashed on the pale Tk+1 box)
style.arrows: many small solid black arrowheads (17), some curved, connecting the task/timing boxes into the inconsistency node and chaining the three scheduler layers
style.font: HelveticaNeue sans, 4.5-7pt, bold for roughly 30% of labels (Prioritize/Abort/Handler headings)

encoding.color_means: rose/dusty-pink = the Tk task instance that is Prioritized; pale pink = Tk+1 marked for Abort; blue-gray = a neutral, unaffected thread or packet; green text = Prioritize; red text = Abort/Inconsistency
encoding.line_style_means: solid arrows carry the decision/data from the timing comparison down through Handler and the three scheduler layers; dashed outline distinguishes the lighter Tk+1 box
encoding.state_means: Prioritized vs Aborted is told apart purely by fill colour (rose vs pale pink) and by the green/red caption text repeated identically at every layer
encoding.marker_means: the letters A, B, C label the two task-instance owners and the comparison node; 'Decision' labels the gate at each layer boundary where the Prioritize/Abort instruction is applied
encoding.emphasis: the same rose/pale-pink colour pair and green/red Prioritize/Abort labels are repeated unchanged at all three scheduler layers, visually proving the decision is consistent end-to-end
reusable_patterns: one decision computed once at the top and re-drawn with identical colour coding at every layer of a stacked system to show consistent propagation
weaknesses: reusing bare letters A/B/C for both task owners and the comparison node, and 'T_k'/'T_k+1' for boxes in four different places, forces the reader to track meaning by position rather than by label

summary: Data-flow Availability proposes tracking a task-and-data-flow graph (TDFG) so that timing-constraint handling stays consistent across the many abstraction layers of an autonomous system's software stack. This figure illustrates Kairos's cross-layer scheduling association for one such decision: two instances of a task (Tk+1, Tk) and a Timing Vertex from a second task feed a comparison node C, which flags an 'Inconsistency' and raises a Prioritize-or-Abort verdict to a top-level Handler. The same verdict, coloured identically (rose for the prioritized Tk, pale pink for the aborted Tk+1), is then re-applied unchanged at three lower layers: the Middleware-level Task Scheduler colours the matching threads inside Thread Pool #1, the Kernel-level Task Scheduler applies it to kernel threads, and the Network Packet Scheduler moves the matching packet ahead in its queue, each behind its own 'Decision' gate.
